packet.headline_seed: Sundar Pichai faces boos, walkout at Stanford graduation ceremony over Google’s Israel, ICE ties
packet.description_seed: AI is once again at the heart of a college graduation protest — this time for the technology's use in Google's defense contracts.

what: Sundar Pichai faces boos, walkout at Stanford graduation ceremony over Google’s Israel, ICE ties

clean_source_blocks.text: The 2026 commencement ceremony at Stanford University was marred by protests against Google CEO Sundar Pichai. As he took the stage, around 200 graduating students staged a walkout, waving Palestinian flags and chanting slogans. The protest was organized by groups like Stanford Students for Justice in Palestine and No Tech for Apartheid. The protesters were specifically targeting Google's contracts with the Israeli government, including Project Nimbus, a $1.2 billion cloud-computing and AI contract signed in 2021.
AI is once again at the heart of a college graduation protest — this time for the technology's use in Google's defense contracts.

Over the weekend, Google CEO Sundar Pichai faced a small revolt when he delivered his commencement speech at Stanford University, where he earned his graduate degree in materials science and engineering. About 200 students from the graduating class reportedly walked out, while others loudly booed the tech executive. The focus of the protest was Google’s defense ties — including Project Nimbus, the controversial $1.2 billion contract, shared with Amazon, to provide cloud and AI services to the Israeli military, as well as its relationship with the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency. ---

Despite the walkout, Pichai continued with his speech at Stanford Stadium. He chose not to mention artificial intelligence (AI) in his address, a topic that has been controversial amid tech layoffs and economic uncertainty. Instead, he urged graduates to "choose optimism, work on hard things, and do what excites you." This decision came after other tech leaders had faced backlash for pro-AI rhetoric during similar events. Stanford grads walk out as Google CEO Sundar Pichai takes the stage as commencement speaker. No mention of AI, unlike other uni speakers getting booed down this year. Story for @sfgate shortly pic.twitter.com/qvS2rJ91Ip

---

[Lähde: NewsBytes]
The 2026 commencement ceremony at Stanford University was marred by protests against Google CEO Sundar Pichai.
As he took the stage, around 200 graduating students staged a walkout, waving Palestinian flags and chanting slogans.
The protest was organized by groups like Stanford Students for Justice in Palestine and No Tech for Apartheid.
The protesters were specifically targeting Google's contracts with the Israeli government, including Project Nimbus, a $1.2 billion cloud-computing and AI contract signed in 2021.

Despite the walkout, Pichai continued with his speech at Stanford Stadium.
    He chose not to mention artificial intelligence (AI) in his address, a topic that has been controversial amid tech layoffs and economic uncertainty.
    Instead, he urged graduates to "choose optimism, work on hard things, and do what excites you."
    This decision came after other tech leaders had faced backlash for pro-AI rhetoric during similar events.

Stanford grads walk out as Google CEO Sundar Pichai takes the stage as commencement speaker. No mention of AI, unlike other uni speakers getting booed down this year. Story for @sfgate shortly pic.twitter.com/qvS2rJ91Ip

Pro-Palestinian activists have slammed Google's contracts with the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF), Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). They allege that these agreements support Israel's military operations.
    After the ceremony, many students attended a separate event called the "People's Commencement," where Algerian-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil was the keynote speaker.
    Khalil had been detained by US immigration authorities for over 100 days due to his pro-Palestinian activism at Columbia University in 2024.

---

[Lähde: Hoodline]
Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai came back to Stanford yesterday as the star of the university’s 135th commencement, addressing the Class of 2026 at Stanford Stadium. His speech leaned into optimism, personal anecdotes and real-world advice, steering clear of the hottest tech battles playing out on campuses. But only a few lines into his remarks, a visible group of graduates stood up, turned away and headed for the exits.

The walkout was organized by campus groups protesting Google’s work with the Israeli government, specifically Project Nimbus. Around 200 students filed out just as Pichai took the stage, while scattered groups in the crowd stayed put and waved banners, blew whistles and raised Palestinian flags, according to SFGATE. Project Nimbus, a roughly $1.2 billion cloud-computing deal that connects Google and Amazon with Israeli government agencies, has been a flashpoint for years of internal dissent and public protest, as detailed by Al Jazeera.

Pichai tried to keep things grounded and practical. He told graduates to run their choices through three filters: choose optimism, take on hard problems and follow what genuinely excites them. AI, the topic many expected him to dwell on, got only a light touch. He joked that it is simply the last two letters of his last name, according to the full transcript posted by Google.

Stanford President Jonathan Levin introduced Pichai as one of the school’s own, pointing to Pichai’s master’s degree from Stanford and framing the day as a kind of homecoming, per the Stanford Report. The contrast between that warm welcome and the students filing out of the stadium was hard to miss.

Many of the graduates who walked out did not just call it a day. They regrouped elsewhere on campus for a separate “People’s Commencement,” an annual alternative ceremony that organizers say is meant to spotlight demands and perspectives the official program ignores. That event featured activist Mahmoud Khalil as a keynote speaker and echoed the same criticisms of Project Nimbus, according to SFGATE. Organizers told The Mercury News that recent graduates, including Eva Jones, played key roles in pulling the event together.

The walkout did not come out of nowhere. It is part of a year of sustained activism at Stanford over Israel and Gaza. But if you’ve been paying attention to the headlines the past few weeks, it’s been an absolute massacre out there on the frontlines of college graduations for any speaker who dares mention AI. payload.title: Googlen toimitusjohtajaa vastustettiin Stanfordin valmistujaisissa
payload.summary: Googlen toimitusjohtaja Sundar Pichai kohtasi buuauksia ja opiskelijoiden ulosmarssin Stanfordin yliopiston valmistujaisissa. Protesti kohdistui Googlen puolustus- ja viranomaissuhteisiin, erityisesti Israelin hallintoon liittyvään Project Nimbus -sopimukseen sekä yhtiön yhteyksiin Yhdysvaltain maahanmuuttoviranomaiseen ICE:en.
payload.content:
Googlen toimitusjohtaja Sundar Pichai kohtasi vastalauseita pitäessään valmistujaispuhetta Stanfordin yliopistossa viikonloppuna. Noin 200 valmistuvaa opiskelijaa poistui paikalta hänen noustessaan lavalle, ja osa yleisöstä buuasi teknologiajohtajalle. Protesti kohdistui Googlen sopimuksiin ja suhteisiin, joiden katsotaan kytkevän yhtiön Israelin hallintoon ja Yhdysvaltain maahanmuuttoviranomaiseen ICE:en.

## Protesti kohdistui Googlen sopimuksiin

Mielenosoittajat arvostelivat erityisesti Project Nimbus -hanketta, jota on kuvattu 1,2 miljardin dollarin pilvilaskenta- ja tekoälysopimukseksi. Sopimus solmittiin vuonna 2021, ja siinä Google sekä Amazon tarjoavat pilvi- ja tekoälypalveluja Israelin hallinnolle ja sotilaallisille toimijoille.

Valmistujaisissa osa opiskelijoista kantoi Palestiinan lippuja ja huusi iskulauseita. Protestia olivat lähdetietojen mukaan järjestämässä muun muassa Stanford Students for Justice in Palestine ja No Tech for Apartheid. Tapaus toi jälleen näkyviin paineen, jota suuret teknologiayhtiöt kohtaavat puolustus- ja viranomaissopimustensa vuoksi.

Pichain esiintyminen oli myös symbolisesti näkyvä, sillä hän on itse suorittanut Stanfordissa materiaalitieteen ja -tekniikan jatkotutkinnon. Tästä huolimatta osa valmistuvista opiskelijoista käytti tilaisuutta julkiseen vastalauseeseen yhtiön liiketoimintasuhteita vastaan.

## Pichai jatkoi puheensa loppuun

Ulosmarssista ja buuauksista huolimatta Pichai jatkoi puhettaan Stanford Stadiumilla. Hän ei lähdetietojen mukaan käsitellyt puheessaan tekoälyä, vaikka aihe on ollut viime vuosina keskeinen osa Googlen julkista profiilia ja samalla kiistanalainen teema teknologia-alan irtisanomisten sekä taloudellisen epävarmuuden keskellä.

Sen sijaan Pichai kehotti valmistuneita valitsemaan optimismin, tarttumaan vaikeisiin asioihin ja tekemään sitä, mikä heitä innostaa. Ratkaisu olla korostamatta tekoälyä erottui tilanteessa, jossa myös muut teknologiajohtajat ovat kohdanneet vastareaktioita tekoälymyönteisistä puheista yliopistojen valmistujaistilaisuuksissa.

Stanfordin tapaus osoittaa, että tekoälyn ja pilvipalvelujen käyttö puolustus- ja viranomaisyhteyksissä on noussut opiskelijaliikkeissä näkyväksi vastustuksen kohteeksi. Samalla se kertoo, että teknologiayhtiöiden johtajat joutuvat yhä useammin vastaamaan julkisesti siihen, mihin niiden järjestelmiä ja sopimuksia käytetään.
summary_bullets: Noin 200 Stanfordin valmistuvaa opiskelijaa marssi ulos Sundar Pichain puheen aikana.
Protesti kohdistui Googlen Israel-sopimuksiin, Project Nimbus -hankkeeseen ja yhteyksiin ICE-viranomaiseen.
Pichai jatkoi puheensa loppuun eikä lähdetietojen mukaan nostanut tekoälyä puheensa aiheeksi.

Over the weekend, Google CEO Sundar Pichai faced a small revolt when he delivered his commencement speech at Stanford University, where he earned his graduate degree in materials science and engineering. About 200 students from the graduating class reportedly walked out, while others loudly booed the tech executive. The focus of the protest was Google’s defense ties — including Project Nimbus, the controversial $1.2 billion contract, shared with Amazon, to provide cloud and AI services to the Israeli military, as well as its relationship with the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency. ---

Despite the walkout, Pichai continued with his speech at Stanford Stadium. He chose not to mention artificial intelligence (AI) in his address, a topic that has been controversial amid tech layoffs and economic uncertainty. Instead, he urged graduates to "choose optimism, work on hard things, and do what excites you."
